fields.sentence: Collectors dry the feathers from sky-cats.

q2_gaps: A DEFINITE-GENERIC plural object inside a generic/habitual clause ("the feathers from sky-cats" = feathers of that kind, not one specific batch). The definite rule is written for a definite "that picks out a specific thing" and the bare-kind filler is reserved for non-specific/generic objects; nothing says which applies when a definite plural is itself kind-referring, and the specific-group encoding makes every collector dry one shared set.
review.notes: Correctly NOT a relational kind-level generic (the object is definite, not a bare kind NP), correctly no (can collect) for the referring-use agent nominalization, and "from sky-cats" takes the entity-attached origin From with the kind constant. Patient on the drying object fits the treatment/physical-change test.

fields.sentence: A handful of ground feathers protects a lantern for about a month.

q1_issues.issue: CardinalityPhrase records "handful" while the instruction set's vague-quantity lexicon lists the phrase as "a handful", so the string may miss the seeded phrase-to-bound rule (the worked example keeps the listed form exactly, "several").

ground_feather is fused but its modifier genus is not exposed, although "ground" is a participial adjective predicable of the referent ("the feathers are ground") and the modifier-genus test is stated as determined, not optional — so either (Inheritance ground_feather ground) is missing or the pair should not have fused at all, per the 'a laminated worktop' treatment.

review.notes: The rest is right: Theme for protect (the lantern is unchanged), a witness group for the vague-quantity indefinite subject, an unmarked event for the dispositional present, and the tight-hedge duration (ParticleFromNormal 1 0.1) at 10% sigma.

issues.reason: The vague-quantity rule requires the phrase 'normalized to the canonical lexicon string', and the only lexicon the instruction set exhibits lists 'a handful' — beside 'a few' and 'a lot of', which likewise keep their leading words — so "handful" is not the canonical form the seeded phrase-to-bound rules key on.

The parse reads 'ground' as a NOUN modifier (feathers from the ground, the fire_exit / night_shift pattern), for which the modifier genus is correctly suppressed; world knowledge picks the reading per Core patterns, every emitted atom is true under it, and the 'laminated worktop' treatment binds only under the participial-adjective reading the parse did not take.

new_gaps: The Cardinality vague-quantity rule requires normalization 'to the canonical lexicon string' but never states the canonicalization itself — whether the leading article is kept — and the one worked example ('several') has none, so 'a few' / 'a handful' / 'a lot of' have no demonstrated canonical form to normalize to.
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form is (CardinalityPhrase sk_group_1 "a handful"), the phrase exactly as the vague-quantity lexicon lists it; nothing else in the parse changes.
adjudication.notes: The remainder is right: Theme for the unchanged lantern, a vague-quantity group witness for the indefinite subject, no status atom on the dispositional present, and the tight-hedge duration at sigma = 10% of the value.
